summary: Helen Moore Johnson was an Indologist who earned degrees at Missouri and Wisconsin, also studying at Tulane, Bryn Mawr, and Johns Hopkins under Maurice Bloomfield. She held teaching posts at Oxford College for Women and Johns Hopkins (1924–1936).

Helen Wang specializes in Sinology, history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. She studied at SOAS University of London (~1984–1988) and became Curator of East Asian Money at the British Museum around 1993.
Helena Blankleder is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She studied under traditional teachers Pema Wangyal Rinpoche and Jigme Khyentse Rinpoche (attested 1999).
Helena Michie studied at the University of Pennsylvania (~1979–1984) and held a post at Rice University around 1990.

Helena Willman-Grabowska was a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. After studying under Baudouin de Courtenay, Lévi, Foucher, Finot, and Meillet, she taught at the University of Paris and was professor at Jagiellonian University (1927–1948).

Helga Uebach was an Indologist and Tibetologist who earned her Ph.D. at the University of Munich under Helmut Hoffmann (~1960–1967). In 1964, she became an editorial consultant at the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities.
Hellfried Dahlmann was a linguist who held academic posts at the University of Marburg (~1935–1952) and the University of Cologne (~1952–1971).

Sinologist Hellmut Wilhelm earned his doctorate at Humboldt University of Berlin under Otto Franke. He taught at Peking University (~1937–1948), worked at the Monumenta Serica Institute, and held the sinology chair at the University of Washington (1948–1971).

Hellmuth Hecker was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Hamburg (PhD ~1945–1948) and under Paul Debes. He served as a Referent at the University of Hamburg from around 1952 to 1988.

Helmer Smith specialized in Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics, studying at Uppsala and under Johansson, Andersen, Bloch, Pischel, and Geldner. He served as Docent of Indology at Lund (1921–1935) and professor at Uppsala (1936–1947).
Helmut Arntz was a linguist who studied under Hermann Hirt (~1930–1934) and held a post at the University of Giessen (~1935–1945).

Helmut Eimer was a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Hamburg, Humboldt University, and Bonn, completing his doctorate under Frank-Richard Hamm (~1968–1973). He held a post at the University of Bonn (~1974–2001).

Helmut Hoffmann was a scholar of Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies who earned his doctorate at Berlin under Heinrich Lüders. He served as professor at Munich (1948–1968) and Indiana University Bloomington (1969–1980).

Helmut Krasser was an Indologist, Tibetologist, and Buddhist studies scholar who completed his Promotion and Habilitation at the University of Vienna. He taught at Vienna (~1990–2014) and directed the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia (2007–2014).

Helmut Nespital studied Indology and linguistics at Humboldt University and Charles University under Vincenc Pořízka. He held posts at Humboldt University (1965–1977), the University of Bamberg (1982), and the Free University of Berlin (1980, 1990).

Helmut Rix studied linguistics and Indology at Heidelberg and Tübingen under Karl Hoffmann. He taught at Augustana Divinity School (1955–1959) and held professorships at the University of Regensburg (1966–1982) and the University of Freiburg (1982–1993).

Helmut Tauscher is a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Vienna under Ernst Steinkellner (Dr. phil. 1981). He served as assistant and associate professor at Vienna (1981–2015) and was a visiting professor at Leiden.

Helmut Uhlig was a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology who studied at the University of Vienna. He taught at the Volkshochschule and became director of Volkshochschule Tempelhof in 1956.

Helmuth Peter Holler was a scholar of religious studies and Indology who studied at Humboldt University of Berlin and Kiel. He served as principal of Rajahmundry Seminary (1897–1900) and was professor and principal at Oriental University (~1903–1923).

Helmuth von Glasenapp studied Indology and religious studies at Tübingen, Munich, Berlin, and Bonn, earning his doctorate under Hermann Jacobi. He held academic posts at Berlin, Bonn, Königsberg (1928–1944), and the University of Tübingen (1946–1959).
